chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs al-Bakhtari, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, a group committed many sins, then they feared them and feared a severe fear. Then others came and said, 'Your sins are upon us.' So Allah sent down punishment upon them. Then He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: 'They feared Me, but you were haughty.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between fearing God and being haughty towards Him according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the spiritual danger of *al-jahd* (presumptuousness) by contrasting a group who feared their sins with those who arrogantly claimed 'your sins are upon us,' thereby assuming divine mercy would cover them regardless of their attitude. This narrative, found in *Thawab al-A'mal*, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis that true repentance requires humility rather than the haughty assumption that one's status guarantees forgiveness, a warning against the sin of being 'haughty against Allah.'

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  narrates  that  a  community  had committed   a   number   of   sins.   However   they   stopped committing them after a period and began to fear those sins a lot. Some people came forward and said, “Your sins are around our necks.” The Almighty Allah sent chastisement on them and said: “Those people used to fear Me and you tried to be haughty.”
